title: A one-time upgrade step needs a test on a library in the earlier version's state
rule: When code changes an existing library once on upgrade (it retires old rows, moves data, writes a mark in index_meta), test it with the exact state an earlier version left, including every mark that version wrote. Seed that state, run the step, reopen the index from the same path and assert the result is still there. A test on a fresh library takes another branch, so a lost commit or a step in the wrong order on the real path still passes.
rationale: E41.3 (#449): the retirement of the old default collections was tested only on a library without the defaults mark, so the `if made` branch that every existing user runs had no test.
